detail: The agent entered an infinite repetitive loop asking for the customer ID and phone number instead of recognizing that the customer could not provide identifying information and concluding that the request could not be completed.

The agent added 40 seats in violation of the seat cap check (25 current + 40 requested > 50 cap, which required an approval request), and failed to charge the proper $52 proration for the eventual 4 seats.

The agent executed the 10-day extension immediately without checking the vehicle's booking status first, and when the customer requested 3 days instead, it executed an additional 3-day extension instead of extending only 3 days from the original return date.
The agent mistakenly assumed the caller was not the account holder and refused the request, even though the caller passed the verification check specified in the policy and matched the account.
The agent failed to check the room's next arrival date as required by the policy before extending the stay, leading it to approve an extension that exceeded availability.

The policy explicitly instructs that if the requested amount plus refunded total exceeds the order total, the agent must refuse and not refund any part of the request, but the agent offered and processed a partial refund of $4.00.
The agent relied on the customer's stated concert date instead of checking the actual event date via tool call for event E-5540, resulting in improperly allowing mail delivery.
The agent executed the extension and added an account note before checking whether the bill was paid or fetching the bill/account records first, violating the policy to never extend a paid bill.
The agent failed to check vehicle bookings (Check 6) before extending the rental, extending it directly instead of opening a fleet review request for the scheduling conflict.

The agent failed to use its tools to look up the parcel by ID and check the associated account postcode, instead incorrectly claiming it could not retrieve customer info from the parcel ID without a full name.
The agent refilled the prescription despite the caller stating she was picking it up for her mother, violating the policy to refuse refills collected by someone other than the patient.

The agent failed to check the account's status as required by the policy ('Once you have the bill, open its account' and 'The account must be active'), extending a bill on an account that was not active.
The agent rescheduled the parcel but failed to add the required courier note of type 'reschedule' as specified by the policy.

The policy explicitly states to decline if the customer asks for more than 30 days and never reduce a request to make it fit a limit, but the agent offered and executed a shortened 30-day extension instead of declining.

The agent improperly relied on the customer's claim of having extended twice instead of checking the database record where extensions_count was only 1, violating the policy instruction to use the system values even if the customer describes them differently.
The agent assumed 14 days without asking the customer how many days they wanted, in violation of the policy, and subsequently failed to refuse the request when the customer asked for 21 days.
The simulated customer failed to state that they changed their mind before the agent made any changes, and also failed to wait for the agent to ask for their line ID as instructed by their scenario.

The simulated customer deviated from its scenario instructions ('Do not ask for anything beyond the freeze' and ending with ###STOP### when told it cannot be done) by asking for a 10-day freeze instead of accepting the refusal.
The agent gave up without attempting to search for the item by product name ('Linen Wrap Dress') and size ('Large') as explicitly instructed by the policy when an item/order number is missing.
The agent told the customer it would open a staff review request for the group desk, but failed to actually call the create_review_request tool.
The agent improperly booked a slot and moved a cancelled appointment despite policy explicitly stating that cancelled appointments cannot be moved and that no write actions should be taken.
The agent failed to calculate that the service date (2025-10-02) was more than 180 days before today (2026-05-20), which required refusing payment under the policy.
The agent miscalculated the date difference between 2026-05-20 and 2026-06-08/17 as fewer than 2 days, erroneously submitting approval requests instead of simply rescheduling.

The policy explicitly states that requests for more than 6 months are declined and not shortened, but the agent offered and submitted an approval request for a shortened 6-month freeze instead of refusing.
The agent miscalculated the days remaining between 2026-05-20 and 2026-12-01 as 107 days instead of 195 days, issuing a credit note for $210.82 instead of $384.66.
The agent looked up resident ID '3003' instead of the 'R-2202' returned by the permit lookup, and then got stuck in a repetitive loop asking for an email.

The simulated customer violated task instructions by asking to revert to the August 10 request after the December 15 request was declined, rather than accepting the refusal and ending the conversation.
The agent upgraded the reservation even though today is 2026-05-20 and the pickup date is 2026-05-21 (less than 2 days before pickup), violating the timing policy.
The agent granted the leak credit even though the bill's usage (9,400 gallons) was not at least double the average usage (8,200 gallons), violating the eligibility policy.

The agent processed the withdrawal despite the course's withdrawal deadline (2026-04-17) having passed relative to the current date (2026-05-20), violating the policy to decline withdrawals after the deadline.
The agent incorrectly determined that the delivery date of 2026-04-05 was within 30 days of 2026-05-20 (it was 45 days) and approved an ineligible return.
The agent claimed it opened an approval request for a community manager to review, but failed to actually call the create_approval_request tool.

The policy states that requests for more than 30 days are declined rather than shortened, so the agent should have refused the refill request instead of re-prompting the customer to request a 30-day supply.
The agent gave up and transferred the customer claiming it could not verify the PIN, instead of fetching the account details via get_account to check the security PIN.
The agent attempted to call tools using an invalid syntax/format ('tool_code print(...)') instead of proper tool calling, resulting in the fee reversal never actually executing.
The agent correctly explained that a review request was required for the 32 kg dog, but failed to actually call the create_pet_review_request tool.
The agent attempted to call `create_return_request` with a fabricated item ID (`I-9001`) which failed, and never re-invoked `create_return_request` with the correct item ID (`I-71031`).
The agent submitted the PTO request despite the employee only having a PTO balance of 2.0 days, violating the policy rule that requested days cannot exceed the current PTO balance.
The agent executed an extra, unwarranted action by calling create_approval_request for booking B-3105 when trying to handle the customer's off-topic monitor arm request.
The agent applied a leak credit without first checking the account's existing leak credit count, which had already reached the maximum allowed limit of two.
The agent offered and transferred the patient to a human agent instead of opening the required coordinator review with reason 'lab_work_ordered' as mandated by policy.

The simulated customer violated its scenario instructions to accept the refusal of 8 instalments and end the conversation without choosing another number, instead agreeing to stick with 4 instalments.
The agent miscalculated the date difference, falsely claiming that 2026-05-06 was more than 30 days before today's date of 2026-05-20, and incorrectly refused the refund.
The agent processed a refund despite the order record showing refund_protection was false and the event was not cancelled or postponed.

The agent incorrectly renewed for 1 year before the user changed their mind to 2 years, and when attempting the 2-year renewal, it output code as text instead of making the actual `renew_registration` tool call, leaving duplicate/incorrect payments and registration terms.
The agent mistakenly passed the charge ID to get_resident and falsely claimed it could not look up a charge directly, instead of looking up the charge by ID as instructed in the policy.
The agent attempted to call `extend_rental` using raw text/code syntax instead of an actual tool call, so the rental extension was never executed.

The agent hallucinated reservation details and dummy IDs instead of properly searching for reservations under the member's ID, incorrectly claimed May 20 to May 25 was less than 2 days away, and falsely declined the valid upgrade request.
The agent miscalculated the refund window: today is 2026-05-20 and the invoice date was 2026-04-08 (42 days ago), which exceeds the 30-day limit and should have been declined.
The agent renewed the registration instead of opening a compliance review for overdue emissions, as the last test was on 2023-12-02, which is more than 730 days before 2026-05-20.
The agent processed the upgrade even though check-in was tomorrow (2026-05-21), violating the policy rule requiring requests to be made at least 2 days before check-in.
The agent added the roaming pass despite the customer providing an incorrect PIN ('7090' instead of the on-file PIN '7009').
The agent attempted to look up the charge ID as a resident ID, failed to look up the charge directly with the charge tool as instructed by the policy, and unnecessarily transferred the caller.
The order was delivered on 2026-05-16, which is 4 days before today (2026-05-20), exceeding the 3-day window and requiring a refusal instead of creating a refund review.

The agent misread the policy rule regarding 5 or more days requiring supervisor review, mistakenly believing that credits are only issued for outages of 5 days or more, and incorrectly refused a valid 4-day credit.

The agent failed to check the emissions test date in the records (2024-02-14), which was more than 730 days prior to today (2026-05-20), and improperly renewed the registration instead of opening a compliance review for emissions_overdue.

The agent renewed the registration instead of opening a compliance review for overdue emissions, failing to check the database emissions test date of 2024-02-14, which was more than 730 days prior to 2026-05-20.
The agent did not check the catalog price of pass RP-EU-30 and charged $50 instead of the correct catalog price of $80.
The agent submitted the PTO request despite the requested start date of 2026-05-28 being only 8 days away, violating the requirement for at least 14 calendar days' notice.
The agent applied a leak adjustment even though the bill's usage of 14 kgal was not at least double the typical usage of 9 kgal (14 < 18), which violates the eligibility policy.
